findings.title: T-1's test needs the CLI red command built in T-10 and T-11
quotes: then red through the CLI with each.
the cargo red exits 1 naming a compile error, with status `claimed`
findings.fix: give T-1 a unit test of `run` and `runner`/`wrong_reason` only. Leave the CLI half of TC-38 with T-11, which already lists TC-38.

sources.situation: a worker takes T-1 with no dependencies and its pack says to make TC-38 pass. TC-38 asserts `implement.runner` and `wrong_reason` and also that `red` through the CLI exits 1 for cargo and 0 for mvn. The `red` command is built in T-10, which T-1 does not depend on, so the worker cannot make the test pass and cannot finish T-1.

findings.reason: TC-38 (tests.md:306-313) ends with "then red through the CLI with each", but T-1 has "Depends on: none" and the `red` command is built in T-10/T-11. T-11 already lists TC-38, and nothing else in tasks.md settles which task owns the CLI half.
findings.note: T-1 names direct unit checks of run, runner and wrong_reason; TC-38's CLI red is proved by T-11

findings.title: T-4's test needs the claim command, which T-4 does not depend on
findings.fix: T-4's `Test:` should cover only the check half (the missing `Mode:` is refused and a legacy list passes). The claim half stays with T-8, which already lists TC-56.

sources.situation: T-4 depends on none and is done first in the order. TC-56 runs `nio check tasks` and then `flow claim`, and asserts the claim prints `mode: split`. The claim command is built across T-3, T-5, T-7 and T-8, all after T-4, so the worker can make the check half pass but not the claim half.

findings.reason: TC-56 (tests.md:419-424) ends with `flow(root, "claim", S)` and asserts "mode: split". T-4 has "Depends on: none" and claim is built in T-7/T-8, which depend on T-4. T-8 already lists TC-56.
findings.note: T-4 names direct checks of tasks.check before and after MODE_SINCE; TC-56's claim half is proved by T-8

findings.title: T-3's test runs claim and green, which are built in later tasks
quotes: Action: three times: `flow(root, "claim", S)`, `write_test(root)`, write passing code
Assert: the claimed tasks are `T-1`, `T-2`, `T-3` in that order.
findings.fix: T-3's `Test:` should name a unit test of `status()` and `next_ready()` over fixture history lines. TC-8 stays with T-21, which already lists it and depends on T-20.

sources.situation: T-3 is pure status derivation and next-ready selection over history lines (no dependencies). TC-8 drives the whole loop through claim, red-free green and review. Those commands come from T-7, T-8, T-13 and T-14, so a worker for T-3 has no passing way to show done.

findings.reason: TC-8 (tests.md:80-85) runs claim, `write_test` and green three times. T-3 has "Depends on: none", and those commands come from T-7, T-8, T-13 and T-14. T-21 already lists TC-8.
findings.note: T-3 names direct checks of status and next_ready on fixture history; TC-8, TC-32 and TC-39 are proved by T-21 (T-2 changed the same way: TC-44 by T-14)

findings.title: T-9's test checks claim output, not the skill file
quotes: it carries the "Talking to the human" block word for word
findings.fix: name a check on the skill file in T-9's `Test:`, for example that it names the five CT-17 steps and passes `tests/test_talk.py`, and add that check to tests.md as its own TC-n.

sources.situation: T-9 writes `skills/implement/SKILL.md`, which CT-17 requires to have five steps and the Talking block. TC-40 only checks that claim prints `mode: direct` and `mode: split`. A skill with no steps and no Talking block passes T-9's test, so the worker cannot tell from its test that it is done.

findings.reason: TC-40 (tests.md:322-327) only asserts the `mode:` line from claim. CT-17 (contracts.md:218-228) requires the skill's steps and the Talking block, and no TC in tests.md checks the steps of `skills/implement/SKILL.md`. `tests/test_talk.py` may cover the Talking block generically, but nothing in the artefact checks the steps, so T-9's test cannot show it is done.
findings.note: T-9's test is tests/test_talk.py plus a direct check of the skill's steps and modes; TC-40 is proved by T-8

findings.title: T-17 serves AC-24 but does not own the card file it tests
quotes: each body contains `never edit` before `state.json` and `history.jsonl`
findings.fix: either add AC-24 to T-6's `Serves:` and TC-24 to its `Test:`, or add `src/nio/agents/worker.md` to T-17's `Files:`.

sources.situation: AC-24 is the card's spec-problem rule (`status: blocked`, `change_request:`, no spec edits). T-17 serves it and its test reads `worker.md`, but T-17's Files do not include `worker.md`. T-6 owns that file and serves only AC-2, and its test (TC-2) checks only the `never edit` text. If T-6 left out the blocked rules, the worker for T-17 would fail TC-24 and would have to edit a file it does not name.

findings.reason: TC-24 (tests.md:205-210) reads `src/nio/agents/worker.md`, but T-17's Files omit that file. T-6 owns the file and serves only AC-2, and TC-2 does not check the blocked-handoff rules. Dependency order does not help: T-17 reaches T-6 through T-11, T-10 and T-8, which only guarantees the file exists, not that it has those rules.
findings.note: AC-24 and TC-24 moved to T-6, which owns worker.md; T-17 serves AC-25 and keeps TC-24 passing
